title: Armature Windings, Pitches & The EMF Equation
subtitle: The armature winding generates EMF in a generator and experiences force in a motor. Understanding lap vs wave winding and the EMF equation is core exam material. You must be able to derive the EMF equation from first principles.

topics.title: Lap vs Wave & The EMF Equation

subtopics.title: Lap vs Wave & The EMF Equation

content.text: Lap winding: parallel paths a = P (number of poles). More paths → more current capacity. High current, lower voltage. Used in large low-voltage machines.
Wave winding: parallel paths a = 2 always, regardless of poles. Two long series strings → higher voltage. High voltage, lower current. Used in high-voltage machines. No equalising connections needed.
Pitches: For simplex progressive lap winding: Yb − Yf = 2. Average pitch: (Yb+Yf)/2 = C/P, so Yb+Yf = 2C/P (C = total coil sides, P = poles).
φ = flux per pole (Wb) · Z = total armature conductors · N = speed (rpm) P = number of poles · a = parallel paths Lap: a = P Wave: a = 2 (always)

Common mistake — Most common mistake in this topic Wrong value of a. For lap: a=P. For wave: a=2 ALWAYS — not 2P, not P/2, just 2. In an 8-pole machine this is a factor of 4 error. Also: Yb+Yf = 2C/P not C/P — the factor of 2 is easy to miss.
